# interfaces — review focus

Contracts nearly every other repo implements against. A change here that looks
small is rarely small.

## OpenAPI annotations are user-facing

`@Schema`, `@Operation`, `@Parameter`, `@ApiResponse` descriptions ship: they
become the public API reference at api.otilm.com, generated by
`interface-documentation`, and the text in generated clients. Review them as
documentation, not as comments.

- A description restating the field name adds nothing, and an overlong one is
  worse here than in a comment because consumers read it.
- **Never move a consumer-relevant constraint off the wire.** Units, ranges,
  nullability, format, defaults and validity rules belong in the annotation
  where a client author will see them. Implementer-facing detail - aggregation
  rules, internal safety obligations, synthesis notes - belongs in the Javadoc,
  which does not ship.
- Flag a Javadoc and an adjacent annotation stating the same thing. They drift,
  and only one of them reaches the consumer.
- A new public field, endpoint or enum value with no description is a
  Documentation finding.

## Contract change blast radius

Adding to an enum, changing nullability, renaming a field or narrowing a type
breaks consumers that this diff does not touch: connectors implementing a
provider contract, and clients of the Core API generated from its published
specification. Say which consumer breaks and how, and prefer Correctness over
Documentation when a change is source- or wire-incompatible.

## Attribute versions

`attributes` v2 is a connector *interface*; attribute *content* has versions v1,
v2 and v3 (`DataAttributeV3`, `RequestAttributeV3`). Every attribute published
by or sent to a v2 connector interface is v3. The wire schema accepts both, but
a v2 content item names no content type, so a Go consumer rejects the whole
request while a Java consumer decodes it silently. A test against a Java
connector or a mock does not show the break: check the wire (`"version":"v3"`
and a `contentType` on every content item). Readers of an attribute once stated
as v2 keep reading both versions.

## Source-compatibility traps

- Adding a field to a DTO with a generated all-args constructor changes the
  constructor every positional caller in another repository compiles against:
  append the field last and keep the previous signature, delegating to the new
  one.
- A numeric field carrying both an inclusive `@Schema` bound and
  `@Positive`/`@Negative` emits conflicting OpenAPI keywords and fails the
  documentation lint in `interface-documentation` while this build stays green;
  use `@Min`/`@Max` beside the bound.
